topics.label: Course introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives for cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional primary modalities of cancer treatment—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their modes of action and clinical limitations.

topics.label: Targeting cancer cell vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies designed to exploit intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the targeting of oncogene addiction using small-molecule kinase inhibitors as well as the molecular mechanisms governing drug resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are utilized to selectively target tumor cell-surface antigens.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and immunotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological basis of immune surveillance against tumors and examine various immunotherapeutic strategies developed to reactivate or engineer T-cell responses.

topics.label: Challenges, progress, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the overarching challenges, historical survival trends, precision medicine approaches, and ethical dilemmas involved in managing cancer.
